cases.title: Elementwise chain
cases.code:
a, b = Tensor.empty(16), Tensor.empty(16)
out = (a*2 + b).relu()
cases.why: Every op has the same 16 RANGE-indexed elements; nothing is realized except the output STORE. One loop, one kernel.

cases.why: The multiply lives *inside* the reduce loop: the REDUCE's own range r1 indexes a and b directly. A reduce never forces its INPUT to be realized.

E_4_2_4

cases.title: Softmax
cases.why: Two reduces (max, then sum of exp) whose results are broadcast back over the row: each reduce result must be complete before it can be broadcast, so each is a kernel. exp(x-max) is a candidate too (two consumers), but it is cheap, so it is recomputed (in K1 for the sum and again in K2 for the output) instead of stored.

kernels.name: r_4_3_8

cases.title: Matmul + bias + relu
cases.code:
a, w, b = Tensor.empty(4, 8), Tensor.empty(8, 3), Tensor.empty(3)
out = (a @ w + b).relu()
cases.why: The matmul is a broadcast-multiply + REDUCE; the bias add and relu are elementwise on the reduce output and are applied at the STORE. One kernel.

cases.title: x - x.mean() (full)
cases.why: Surprise: ONE kernel. The full mean has shape (), so it has no output ranges to realize; the reduce is simply evaluated inside the output kernel (and codegen hoists it out of the loop).

cases.title: contiguous() forces a split
cases.why: contiguous() is a STAGE; prepare_rangeify turns it into a STORE into a fresh ALLOC (stage_to_anon_store). A STORE is always realized and never removed: two kernels.

cases.title: A tensor used twice
cases.why: y has two consumers that iterate it with different reduce ranges, so it is a realize candidate — but storing y*3 costs more than recomputing one multiply, so pm_remove_bufferize removes it: both reduces read the input and multiply again. One kernel.

cases.title: assign with a hazard
cases.why: Element i reads element 7-i of the buffer it is overwriting: a write-after-read hazard. realize_store_after_src realizes the source first (dest is in the source's toposort), so the flipped values are written to a temporary first: two kernels.

kernels.name: E_2_4

cases.title: COPY between devices
cases.why: A COPY is an anonymous STORE into a buffer on the destination device (copy_to_anon_store). The cross-device STORE first needs its source materialized on CPU:1, and later becomes a CALL(STORE) — a bulk copy, not a compiled kernel.

cases.title: MAX_KERNEL_BUFFERS=4
cases.code:
ts = [Tensor.empty(16) for _ in range(6)]
out = ts[0]+ts[1]+ts[2]+ts[3]+ts[4]+ts[5]
# run with MAX_KERNEL_BUFFERS=4
cases.why: pm_limit_bufs counts the buffers each binary op reaches; past MAX_KERNEL_BUFFERS-1 inputs it inserts a fresh bufferize (stage()) on its elementwise sources. Devices like WEBGPU (8 bindings) need this; on CPU it is off unless you set the variable.
